initial_prompt: What's the difference between a virus and bacteria?

messages.content: What's the difference between a virus and bacteria?

Viruses and bacteria are fundamentally different types of microorganisms. Bacteria are living cells - complete, self-sufficient organisms that can reproduce on their own, have their own metabolism, and exist independently. Viruses aren't really "alive" in the traditional sense - they're just genetic material (DNA or RNA) wrapped in a protein coat that can only reproduce by hijacking a host cell's machinery.

This difference matters practically: antibiotics work against bacteria by disrupting their cellular processes, but are useless against viruses since viruses don't have those processes to disrupt.
